newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL to re-organise employee unit trust.
newsitem.headline: FCL to re-organise employee unit trust.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Ltd said on Thursday it was to re-organise its employee unit trust, cutting the trust's shareholding in the company to 2.7 percent from 11.7 percent by unwinding most of its holding in Fletcher's four listed divisions.
A NZ$695 million loan which funded the trust's holdings in Fletcher Paper, Energy, Building and Forests would be repaid.
The share sale would be priced at market.
Any surplus left over once the $695 million had been repaid would remain in the trust. The surplus was expected to be about 2.7 percent of Fletcher's capital, valued at about $180 million.
The shares purchased would be held as treasury stock and have no voting or dividend rights.
The trust would then have no debt.
The transaction is not expected to have any financial impact on the group, the company said in a statement.
But spokesman Barry Akers said it was possible it might have a positive impact on the share price.
He said analysts had viewed the trust negatively as adding complexity to understanding the company, and being seen as a vehicle for perpetuating the current management.
Chief Financial Officer Ian Donald was quoted as saying he believed the reorganisation would be welcomed by shareholders.

"Some equity market commentators have viewed the unit trust as an unwelcome complexity with perceived impications for control of the group and an overhang of shares that might one day come to the market."

In order to remove the retained interest the Building, Energy and Paper Division of Fletcher Challenge hold in the Forests division, beyond that retained by the Trust, the board decided that these three divisions will bonus four Forests shares for every 100 Building, Energy and Paper shares held.
Using a market value of $2.00 per forest share, this would represent an 8 cents per share dividend.
